title: vicia tenuifolia subsp. subalpina
intro: Vicia tenuifolia subsp. subalpina, commonly known as Alpine Vetch, is a plant species that belongs to the pea family (Fabaceae). It has been traditionally used for its medicinal properties, which include relieving respiratory issues such as bronchitis and coughs due to its expectorant and anti-inflammatory properties. The bioactive constituents of Alpine Vetch include flavonoids, alkaloids, and saponins, which contribute to its therapeutic actions, including antioxidant, antimicrobial, and antispasmodic effects. The plant's health benefits are attributed to its ability to alleviate symptoms of respiratory diseases, as well as its potential to reduce inflammation and improve digestion.
